source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Identify yourself after beginning care, then move personal items as needed without describing the changes because touch will help the client locate them later.","B":"Use touch to announce your presence and rely mainly on gestures during care because verbal descriptions provide little benefit when vision is impaired.","C":"Speak primarily to a companion about the environment and procedures because the companion can later explain visual details to the client afterward.","D":"Identify yourself when entering, provide adequate lighting, read pertinent information aloud, and describe locations of important items verbally as needed."}}
source_row.rationale: Communication with visual impairment should maximize verbal orientation and accessible information. Option D is correct because the nurse identifies self, provides appropriate lighting, reads pertinent information aloud, and verbally describes item locations. Option A moves belongings without orientation. Option B relies on gestures that the client may not see. Option C unnecessarily redirects communication to a companion rather than the client.
